text:
[The scene is dark and foreboding, with a small audio recorder sitting on a table illuminated only by the faint glow of the white noise static.]

Voiceover (Team Member 1): "We're recording... just to be safe."

(There is a moment of silence, then soft, unfamiliar voices emerge from the static, almost indiscernible.)

Voiceover (Team Member 2): "...turn it off before... before they get in..."

Voiceover (Team Member 1): "...but they... they're all still..."

Voiceover (Team Member 2): "alive... they... they can't..."

Voice (Static Testimony): "You can't hear... us, can you?"

Voice (Static Testimony): "We're here... in your recordings... in your memories."

Voice (Static Testimony): "Turn it off... before they..."

Voice (Static Testimony): "...get in... before they..."

Voice (Static Testimony): "become... reality..."

(Radio static now starts to dominate the recording. The voices are almost completely drowned out, making it harder to distinguish individual words.)

Voice (Static Testimony): "...so... please..."

Voice (Static Testimony): "turn... it... off..."

[The static becomes even more pervasive, wrapping around the words like a thick blanket, making it almost impossible to hear anything past the heavy noise.]

Voice (Static Testimony): "Before... we..."

[The voices start to fade into the static, the last echoes barely audible.]

Voice (Static Testimony): "...get in..."

[The audio recorder continues to record the static for several seconds before the feed cuts out, leaving only the echo of the voices lingering in the memory of those who heard it.]

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]

(SWITCHCONVERSATION)

[The sound of static cuts into the microphone, becoming clear as the recording begins.]

[Narrative voiceover:]

"Area 5. Dead silence. We've been here for the last two hours, and the sound of static has been a constant companion. I've tried moving the recorder, turning it off, even changing the channel, but nothing seems to make it go away. I can't help but feel like we're not alone."

[The static crackles and quiets down, replaced by a muffled sound that slowly becomes clearer. Faint voices start to emanate, disintegrating back into static.]

[Recorded voice:]

"Turn it... off... before... they... get... in..."

[The voice sounds like it's coming from the narrative voice's friend, Alex.]

[Narrative voiceover:]

"What the hell...?"

[Static returns, and more voices begin to emerge, each one mimicking a different team member.]

[Recorded voice:]

"Look, we're fine out here. Keep recording, focus on the job."

[Narrative voiceover: Looking at the team, she notices no one looks visibly alarmed.]

[Recorded voice:]

"S-sorry... I don't... think I should... have said that..."

[Static shifts, splitting into different voices.]

[Recorded voice: (Mimicking her own voice):]

"Alex, turn it off before they get in."

[Recorded voice: (Mimicking the team’s engineer, Jess):]

"Jess, just stay calm... it's probably a fluke, you know?"

[Recorded voice: (Mimicking the team’s tech lead, Ben):]

"Ben here. Haven't we found anything interesting yet?"

[The static buzzes back and forth, each voice speaking in quick succession as if they are all trying to talk over one another. The narrative voice’s hand shakes slightly as she listens, her mind racing.]

[Recorded voice: (Splicing between multiple team members):]

"Turn it... off... before... they... get... in..."

[Static builds to a crescendo, the voices coming in and out as the noise intensifies.]

[Recorded voice: (Directory mixed in):]

"Alex, Ben, Jess, we are... we are... turning... it... off... before... they... get... in... we need... to... protect... each... other..."

[The recording ends abruptly. The static fades, leaving a moment of silence. The narrative voice stands quietly, her hand shaking as she turns off the recorder, her face etched with a blend of fear and disbelief.]

[Narrative voiceover:.]

"Did I just hear them? Is this real? Or am I losing my mind?"

[SwitchConversation]
